title: Swimmer drowning South Beach Skerries
description: Swimmer drowned at South Beach in shallow surf after rip formed near the groyne. NE wind 15kts, swell 1.4m, spring tide. RNLI Skerries recovered casualty.

title: Two teenagers rescued Skerries Harbour
description: Two teenagers swept off pier by wave. NE swell 1.6m, wind ENE 12kts, spring tide surge. Rescued by RNLI ILB.

title: RNLI Skerries callout — swimmer in difficulty
description: Swimmer in difficulty 200m offshore. ESE wind 14kts, swell 1.2m, spring tide ebb. RNLI towed to safety.

title: Paddleboarder rescued off Skerries Island
description: Paddleboarder carried offshore in wind shadow eddy. NE 20kts, tide ebbing fast. Coast guard helicopter. Swell 1.0m.

title: Father and son kitesurfers rescued off South Beach Skerries — hypothermia
description: Shortly before 4:30pm, Dublin Coast Guard received an emergency call reporting kitesurfers unable to return to shore off the south beach in Skerries. Skerries RNLI Atlantic 85 'Louis Simson' found two men — a father and son — in the water holding on to a kitesurfing board. Both were helped aboard. Volunteers assessed their condition; both showed early signs of hypothermia. An ambulance was requested and one of the men was transferred to hospital for further monitoring and treatment.

title: Multi-agency search for missing swimmer at Portrane — false alarm
description: Shortly after 12pm on Sunday 12 January, Dublin Coast Guard received a 999 call reporting a swimmer diving into the water near the Martello tower in Portrane (approximately 10 km south of Skerries) but not resurfacing. Skerries RNLI Atlantic 85 'Louis Simson', Howth Coast Guard RIB, Rescue 116 helicopter, and Skerries Coast Guard volunteers carried out an extensive search. Shortly before 3pm, with nothing found and no information regarding anyone missing, the Coast Guard declared it a false alarm with good intent.

title: Two paddleboarders struggling at Kelly's Bay Skerries — RNLI stood by
description: Several 999 calls were made to Dublin Coast Guard reporting two people on a paddleboard struggling to return to shore off the rocks at Kelly's Bay in Skerries. Skerries RNLI had a visual on the paddleboarders from the moment the lifeboat left the station. Once alongside, the paddleboarders confirmed they did not need direct assistance but acknowledged that conditions were changing. The lifeboat stood by until they made their way safely ashore.

title: Mother and child on paddleboard rescued off Balbriggan by Skerries RNLI
description: Shortly after 8pm, Skerries RNLI volunteers were tasked by Dublin Coast Guard following 999 calls reporting a mother and child on a paddleboard being blown out to sea approximately one mile north of Bremore Point in Balbriggan, some 200 metres offshore. Both were taken on board the lifeboat along with their paddleboard.
